validators.label: T85: the companion's persona choice must actually be DELIVERED, and the gate that proves it was never being run (registered 2026-08-31). tools/companion_delivery_gate.py has existed and PASSES standalone - persona_resolution current=0 baseline=0 - but it appeared ZERO times in this file, so the board never executed it. T85 sat at `locking` 90% naming `companion-delivery` in its artifacts, and validate_trajectory_registry let that stand because rule 5 requires a `locking` row to NAME a gate without checking the name RESOLVES. So the registry asserted a lock, the script existed, the script passed - and nothing connected the three. ★THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS FOUND TWICE MORE TODAY, which is why it is worth a long label: 96 psql recipes carried a `replay` line and nothing ever re-ran them (fixed by the psql-probe-suite gate), and 16 of 20 locked trajectories rest on gates reading SKIP because full boards were dying on KeyError: 'args'. A lock nothing runs locks nothing, and the three failure modes are indistinguishable from the outside - unregistered, unrun, and skipped all look exactly like green. The gate itself is the pre-existing companion delivery check (persona resolution against its baseline); registering it is the whole fix, and it makes T85's claim true rather than aspirational.

T182: a message shown too briefly was never shown. A toast is how this platform says 'saved', 'not saved', 'you cannot do that yet' - the entire receipt for most actions - and a receipt that vanishes before it can be read is WORSE than none, because the action looks silent so the person repeats it. Not hypothetical here: the recorded incident had nine REFUSALS displayed for zero milliseconds, i.e. never displayed at all, on exactly the paths where the user most needed to know why they were stopped. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the class is EXTINCT: 937 showToast calls, 906 on their page's default and 31 with an explicit duration, all between 4000 and 7000ms; every one of the 27 per-page showToast implementations holds its toast 2200-3500ms; nothing anywhere is under 1500ms. TWO ASSERTIONS, guarding an absence rather than fixing a present defect: no call passes an explicit duration below the floor, and no implementation holds its message for less. ★THE FLOOR IS 1500ms AND DELIBERATELY LOW - this gate does not litigate whether 3000 beats 3500, a judgement 27 pages have already made sensibly and which a gate would only turn into enforced taste; it catches what is objectively broken, a message a human cannot finish reading. ★THE CENSUS PARSES ARGUMENTS RATHER THAN SCANNING A WINDOW, and that is the lesson: a first version looked for the nearest ', <number>)' after each call and reported ten short toasts, EVERY ONE FALSE - it had matched slice(0, 24), setTimeout(..., 60) and other numerics belonging to different calls entirely, including a '24ms toast' in utils.js that does not exist. Only balanced-paren splitting knows which arguments belong to which call. Teeth proven on both assertions.

T42 (critic deepwalk): MODALS TRAP BACK. Walked live: opening inventory's Add-Part modal pushed no history entry, so the phone hardware-Back gesture navigated away from the WHOLE page mid-form (inventory -> logbook, task + typed input gone); no page implemented modal-back-to-close. Fixed in the ONE shared primitive every hand-rolled modal already opts into (whModalA11y/whSheetA11y): activate() pushes {whModalBack:true}, a shared popstate handler closes the TOP open modal via its OWN close path (the same logic Escape uses), and deactivate() consumes the entry with a suppressed history.back() when the modal closed any other way (X/backdrop/save) so no ghost states accumulate. Proven live on the walked defect: Back dismissed the modal and STAYED on inventory; after an X-close the stack drained (next Back exits cleanly). 2026-10-12 (UFAI W4791): the give-back history.back() reached every OTHER popstate listener as if the person pressed Back - skillmatrix's Take Exam opened the exam and two listeners closed it at once (the exam could not be taken); teaching only those sent the click to index.html, because Chrome resolves the back() before the exam's push. Now: the give-back is deferred a task and issued as ONE counted whBookkeepingBack(n), a modal opening in the same turn takes the entry over, and EVERY popstate listener in a shipped page asks whIsBookkeepingBack() first (or is marked wh-popstate-reconciler). Gate: 5 utils legs + a scan of every shipped popstate listener; self-test reddens on each leg and on a planted naked or named listener.

Critic-deepwalk T42 lock: hardware Back closes an open modal instead of leaving the page, through ONE owner per modal. Walked live at 390 (2026-09-02): inventory's Add-Part modal pushed NO history entry, so the phone Back gesture navigated inventory -> logbook, losing the worker's mid-form input. 2026-10-12 (UFAI W4791 follow-through): two owners was the next defect - whModalHistory AND whModalA11y each pushed an entry for that modal (its X/Cancel never gave whModalHistory's back), whOverlayBackDismiss pushed a third kind for every overlay whSheetA11y also wires (an X-close left a Back that did nothing), and marketplace's empty backdrop divs were wired as dialogs (one Back closed only the backdrop; the sheet stayed open). Now: whModalHistory retired, inventory wired by whModalA11y alone, whOverlayBackDismiss owns only unwired overlays, and an empty scrim hands its role and entry to its sibling .sheet. Measured live on skillmatrix, inventory and marketplace. Teeth: each of the five shapes reddens alone.

No placeholder written as a bare tag in served markup (critic batch, 2026-10-13). marketplace-seller's hint said buyers reach you at m.me/<your-handle>: the parser read <your-handle> as an element and rendered nothing, so sellers read 'opens m.me/ directly' while the source looked right to every reviewer. Every start tag in the 229 served pages must be an HTML, SVG or MathML element (the platform defines no custom elements); scripts, styles and comments are skipped. Teeth: HEAD's marketplace-seller fails at line 453. Markup built in JS strings is not covered.

CRITIC DEEPWALK anti-drift: the UI/UX extension's critique bank cannot overstate. critic_registry.json (480 rows, one per in-scope trajectory) is the SSOT behind the roadmap header's '-> CRITIC DEEPWALK <pct>%' pointer line; this gate holds it to the same discipline as the trajectory registry: R1 structure/status vocabulary; R2 honesty (a critiqued row carries graded dims or a clean_note, walked rows carry walked_at, findings carry dim/layer/severity/evidence/owner); R3 coverage (every in-scope trajectory exactly once, descoped ids absent); R4 dimension vocabulary (a finding on a dim the rubric spec does not define is instrument drift); R5 walkability (pages or an explicit no_ui_basis). Teeth: hollow-critique, invented-dim, dupe, silent-drop and descoped-present all redden in --self-test. Registered 2026-09-02 when the extension landed at root - the same change that taught momentum_stop_guard the critic queue (the star-x16 lesson: the target grew, the bind must grow WITH it).

A ratchet on DEVICE-CLOCK day boundaries (2026-10-13). WorkHive's day is the Manila day, and four critique rows the same day found code taking 'today', 'now', a greeting or 'since midnight' from the device instead (dayplanner 8 sites, hive 3, pm-scheduler, project-report) - on Ian's own New Zealand host, and on the home page itself, whose 'today' window for get_hive_dashboard opened at 19:00 Manila the day before (fixed and walked on an Auckland and a London clock: p_day_start is Manila midnight on both). Counts, in code with comments stripped, on every production page and root shared script: setHours(0,0,0,0), toISOString().slice(0,10), toLocaleDateString with no timeZone, new Date().getHours/getDay/getDate. 150 sites in 20 files on the day it was built (89 were engineering-design.js report date stamps), all cleared the same day - pinned to Manila through the new utils.js whManilaYmd / whManilaMidnight, or marked device-clock-allow where the math was already Manila or pure UTC date arithmetic; the baseline is 0, so ANY new device-clock day boundary fails. 'device-clock-allow: <why>' marks a site that really means the viewer's clock, or local-field math on a date already shifted to Manila. Teeth: the pre-fix pm-scheduler daysLabel reddens; each pattern bites its own shape; Manila-pinned, commented and allow-marked forms do not.

T146: a hang must END, not spin forever. A fetch to an AI or transcription edge function is the one a plant floor will hang - a dead spot, a cold function, a slow uplink - and without a bound there is no failure at all, just a control stuck in its working state saying nothing. That is the eternal-skeleton shape wearing a spinner, and it is worse than an error because an error at least tells someone what to do next. THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN: written after finding voice-journal's transcribeBlob unbounded, it immediately found THREE MORE - report-sender's transcribe, voice-handler's transcribe, and analytics' ORCHESTRATOR, the longest-running call on the platform, where a supervisor waiting on a report could not tell 'still thinking' from 'never coming back'. All four now route through the platform's own fetchWithTimeout rather than a second hand-rolled controller: it already owns the AbortController, the transport-retry policy and the null-on-abort contract. ★THE BOUNDS ARE SIZED FOR THE SLOWEST LEGITIMATE SUCCESS, NOT A DEVELOPER'S PATIENCE - 45s for a long spoken entry over a weak uplink, 120s for a full AI analytics phase - because a timeout tuned short turns working software into a lottery for the plants furthest from the server. Deliberately scoped to slow-by-nature endpoints: a quick REST read is already covered by whQueryTimeout, and demanding a timeout on every call in the codebase would be noise. ★CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (T40): this gate accepted a bare AbortController or a bare `signal:` as proof of a bound — and those are a CANCEL BUTTON, somewhere for a person to press, not a clock that fires on its own. analytics-report carried both and was still unbounded: the 22-page retry sweep graded it SILENT, sitting on 'Compiling analytics across all 4 phases' forever under a read outage because nothing would ever abort it if the reader simply waited — and this gate passed that page every run. A real bound now requires a TIMER: fetchWithTimeout, AbortSignal.timeout, a setTimeout that calls abort, or a Promise.race against a timed promise. The controller may still sit beside those (it is how the abort is delivered) but can no longer stand in for them. A --selftest pins all five cases, the first being the pre-fix analytics-report source, which must be RED.

T172: the terms may not promise what the product lacks. terms-of-service said, in two places, 'You may export your data at any time and delete your account' and 'You may stop using WorkHive and delete your account at any time'. NEITHER SURFACE EXISTS - there is no export-my-data control (T77) and no account-deletion door (T164). A marketing page overclaiming is bad; a TERMS page overclaiming is a promise at legal weight, made to a Philippine user exercising a PDPA right, and it is the document they would point to. THE FIX WAS NOT TO DELETE THE RIGHT: the right is real and the privacy policy already documents how it is honoured - email admin@workhiveph.com with the subject 'Data Rights Request'. The terms now say exactly that, and say plainly it is handled by hand rather than through a button. Same right, true sentence. Both the HTML and its .md twin were corrected, because a promise surviving in either copy is a promise still unkept. THE ASSERTION: no legal surface may claim a SELF-SERVE capability the product does not have - and each banned phrasing is PAIRED WITH THE CONTROL that would make it true, so the day somebody ships account deletion the claim becomes allowed by the same gate that forbids it now. NOT A PROSE LINT: it checks specific self-serve promises against specific missing controls, because a gate that graded legal writing would produce false reds forever and teach everyone to ignore it. Resurrection: RED on all three pre-fix claims.

T198: an 'it could not be computed' branch must be REACHABLE. A page that distinguishes 'computed, and the answer is nothing' from 'we could not compute it' has done the hard part of honest degradation - so the failure this catches is subtler and worse than not having the branch: the branch EXISTS, somebody wrote it deliberately, and the fallback hands it a value that can never trigger it. THE INSTANCE THAT PROVED THE CLASS: project-manager's renderCpm() guards `if (!cp)` and prints 'The critical path could not be computed right now', while its client fallback returned critical_path: { item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {} } - AN EMPTY OBJECT IS TRUTHY, so the guard never fired on the path it was written for, and a shutdown project whose real schedule is '12d, 7 of 7 items on the critical path' rendered as 'CRITICAL PATH 0d - 0 of 7 items' with a full Gantt beneath it. Fixed with critical_path: null. THE ASSERTION: where a consumer's if (!x) branch says something could not be computed, no producer in that file may assign x an empty-but-truthy value - measured at 11 such guards platform-wide and ZERO defeated, so the CLASS is extinct rather than the one instance being patched. ★AN EMPTY ARRAY AS A PLAIN DEFAULT IS NOT THIS: parts: [], rows: [], work: [] are correct ways to say 'none', and a first sweep flagged 33 of them; what makes it a defect is a consumer that DISTINGUISHES uncomputed from empty and a producer that collapses the distinction. ★AND THE DETECTOR FAILED ITS OWN RESURRECTION TEST FIRST - its producer pattern could not match a value containing nested braces, and the real defect contained slack_per_item: {}, so it reported 0 with the bug present. A detector that cannot find the bug it was written for is worse than none; it now allows one nesting level and is proven to go 1 -> 0 across the fix.

Prod headers cover what ships (Content-Security-Policy must permit every external script/stylesheet the pages load and every requirement written into the source; Permissions-Policy must permit every browser API they call — an empty allowlist like geolocation=() denies our own pages too. _headers has no local equivalent, so all of it fails only in production, silently)

Status literals are classified (every status value the code WRITES must be one the consuming truth view classifies — a value permitted by a CHECK but bucketed by nothing is a value that means nothing)

T46/T105: ask for push when the worker WANTS it. A notification prompt at first paint is the fastest way to lose the permission permanently - the person has no reason to say yes yet, they say no, and the browser remembers that answer forever with no in-app way to undo it. There is no second chance, so WHEN the prompt fires matters more than how the feature is built. MEASURED - two call sites, both exemplary: marketplace-seller's svcEnablePush() runs from an onclick ('Turning on…') behind online/support/signed-in checks and refuses honestly when the answer is no ('Alerts stay off until you allow notifications'); voice-handler's _requestPushPerm() fires ONLY when the worker has VERBALLY opted in (_isPushOptInReply) and only while the state is still 'default', inside the open user-gesture window, so a prior denial is never re-prompted. TWO ASSERTIONS: every requestPermission() sits behind a permission-state check or an explicit user action, and no call site is reachable from a load-time path. ★A LOOKBACK WINDOW CANNOT SEE A GESTURE BINDING, and the first version proved it by calling a correctly-gated prompt 'bare': svcEnablePush IS bound to an onclick 350 lines earlier, far outside any sane window. The binding is a property of the enclosing FUNCTION, not of nearby text, so the gate now resolves the function name and asks whether the file wires it to a click anywhere - the same structural-over-proximity correction that keeps coming up. ★IT CHECKS THE ASK, NOT THE FEATURE: whether push is wired, which VAPID key, whether the message is good all belong elsewhere; this is only about the one moment that cannot be taken back. Teeth proven with an injected DOMContentLoaded prompt.

T117 / WCAG 2.5.7: nothing may become reachable ONLY by dragging. A worker in gloves, a person with a tremor and anyone on a trackpad share one need - no function should require a dragging movement. The census found the platform CLEAN, and every gesture it has is harmless: nav-hub and companion-launcher let a person DRAG the floating button out of the way while opening it stays a TAP; session-timeout listens for touchstart as an activity SIGNAL, not a gesture requirement; wh-persona sets draggable=false, disabling dragging rather than requiring it. The one genuine keyboard trap in this family was already closed centrally - .wh-scroll-x regions scrolled by swipe were unreachable from a keyboard (axe scrollable-region-focusable, eight on project-report), fixed where the shared class lives rather than per call site. THE GATE FOUND A HIT ON ITS FIRST RUN and it was checked rather than assumed: integrations.html registers a drop handler for CMMS imports - and it is guarded by if (dropZone && fileInput), with a real labelled input type=file wired to the SAME handleFile on change. Drag-and-drop over a working file picker is exactly what 2.5.7 asks for, so it is justified by name with that reason recorded. A NEW gesture file fails - not because dragging is forbidden, but because 'is there a tap that does the same thing?' is a question somebody must answer out loud before it ships. Scoped to product surfaces: vendor bundles and the measurement tooling whose JOB is to find drag handlers are excluded, since a lens that greps for dragstart would otherwise fail a gate about dragstart. ★MERGED WITH T75 (2026-08-26), which asked the same question of dayplanner and found it has NO drag machinery at all - the walk's premise was wrong, there was no drag to alternate. That pass added the rule that now decides the FAB repositioners: a handler assigning only style.left/right/top/bottom MOVES a control and confers no capability, so it passes, while one that also mutates data (insert, splice, sort_order) is load-bearing and must offer a tap. Deciding by what the handler WRITES rather than by which file it lives in keeps the exemption from becoming a licence. ★AND A REAL MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: driving T75 I wrote a second version of this gate straight over the T117 file, having read 'updated successfully' as 'created', then removed 102 unrelated gate registrations with an over-greedy cleanup regex. The duplicate-id guard caught the first, a HEAD diff caught and repaired the second. A duplicate id is a signal to MERGE two efforts, never to register the same name twice.

T176: whReadError's second argument is SPLICED MID-SENTENCE (2026-08-27). The helper does not print `what` — it composes 'Your session expired, so ' + thing + ' could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it.' — so it must receive a NOUN PHRASE ('your equipment list', 'the audit log'). Four callsites passed a whole SENTENCE, and what shipped was: "Your session expired, so Could not load your equipment list. Check your connection. could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it. Nothing you did was lost." MEASURED in the browser, not reasoned — the same call with a noun returns the sentence it should. ★THE MISTAKE HAD A GOOD MOTIVE, which is why it needs a gate and not a scolding: each site was CONVERTED from a hand-rolled message to the taxonomy helper — exactly the right move — and the old sentence was forwarded into the argument slot. logbook even carries a comment above it explaining that the upstream sentence belongs in console.error and never in the notice; the author understood the principle and still handed the helper a sentence. Converting to the taxonomy means REPLACING the sentence with a noun, not passing it through. ★AND IT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER CHECK: the helper is present, so an adoption sweep passes it; the string holds no raw error text, so the raw-echo ratchet passes it; nothing throws. Only reading the composed sentence shows it — and that sentence only appears when a session dies mid-read, which is precisely when nobody is watching. whWriteError and whAiError are OUT OF SCOPE by design: their second argument IS a fallback message. Teeth (--selftest, 7 cases) incl. both out-of-scope helpers and a verb-opener with no period. Static, read-only.

T105: a table the UI writes should have a READER (2026-08-27). The table-level twin of captured-columns-reach-a-reader — that one asks which COLUMNS never reach a person, this asks which whole TABLES the UI fills and never opens again. ★IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN: marketplace-seller writes push_subscriptions when a provider enables job alerts and never reads one back, and the push card renders only while `Notification.permission !== 'granted'` — so the moment permission is granted the card vanishes forever and NOTHING ever confirms a subscription row exists. Browser permission and a live subscription are different facts: the endpoint rotates, the service worker is replaced, an upsert fails, a row is cleared, and permission stays 'granted' through every one of them — leaving the provider shown nothing while believing the page's own promise that they will 'hear new hails with this tab closed'. Measured at 0 rows. The table having no reader is precisely what let the page never check; the fix gave the card a third state ('granted but not actually subscribed', with a one-tap repair) and thereby gave the table its reader. ★READS THROUGH VIEWS COUNT, and that is the whole difficulty: naively 14 of 54 written tables looked write-only, including community_posts, hives and service_requests — all read constantly, through TRUTH VIEWS (community reads v_community_posts_truth). Resolving view→base-table from information_schema took 14 down to 2, and both survivors were real. A sweep that cannot see through a view manufactures a dozen false findings. ★A FAILED READ MUST NOT ACCUSE: the page's lookup returns null for UNKNOWN and only an explicit false warns, so a refused read can never tell a correctly-subscribed provider their alerts are off. Ratchet: the one survivor (early_access_emails — service_role-only RLS, an Ian decision on T67) is baselined with its reason. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. the view-resolution case in both directions. Needs the local DB for the view map; SKIPs rather than guesses when it is down.

T15: a column written for a PERSON must reach one (2026-08-27). logbook captured loto_applied, permit_reference, readings_json and failure_consequence on its form, stored them on the row, restored them into the EDIT FORM when an entry was edited, and rendered them to a reader NOWHERE — 1,767 of 3,811 entries carried equipment readings nobody could see. ★THE PHANTOM-COLUMN AUDITOR CANNOT CATCH THIS: it asks whether a column has a READ CONSUMER, and a `.select('loto_applied')` satisfies it. SELECTED IS NOT RENDERED — that gap is the whole finding. Asked platform-wide over 121 written columns it returned 9, and project_roles.assigned_by was a real one: 36 of 36 rows record who assigned a project role and the pill showed the name alone, so 'who put me on this?' had no answer in the app (fixed; the sweep now confirms it dropped off the list). A RATCHET, not a cliff — the survivors are baselined WITH their verdicts, because the triage is the valuable part. THREE are FIXED and deliberately absent from the baseline so a regression fails this gate: assigned_by, variance_reason (the provider's finished-job card now reports the amount, method, reference and the payer's reason) and provider_type (the quote card now says 'Hive team' or 'Freelancer' where a buyer chooses). Of the rest: 3 are NOT defects (timestamps whose fact the rendered status already carries; a total the page shows as its two parts), 2 are unused rather than withheld (MEASURED at 0 rows — live_location has never been populated, so no client is being denied it), and 1 is a raw auth uid whose display would trade this defect for the no-raw-internals one. ★SCOPE IS PLATFORM-WIDE ON PURPOSE: per-page it reported ~30 false candidates, because pages WRITE audit rows (actor/target_id/target_name/target_type) and the AUDIT-LOG page renders them. ★AND WRITERS ≠ RENDERERS: shared scripts count as renderers so a column shown by utils.js is not 'invisible', but treating them as writers too pulled in ten AI-telemetry columns (response_time_ms, model_confidence…) written for a machine, not a person. Credential columns (key_hash, p256dh, auth uids) are excluded outright — not rendering those is the security property. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. cross-page rendering, form-restore-is-not-rendering, and secrets. Static, read-only.

Storage-Key Registry (PLATFORM_CENTRALIZATION C-P4: every localStorage/sessionStorage key is CANONICAL or a registered ALIAS in storage_key_registry.json; a new UNKNOWN key FAILs until registered — stops the wh_active_hive_id/wh_hive_id drift class)

Client RBAC Ratchet (PLATFORM_CENTRALIZATION +RBAC: raw `role === 'supervisor'` comparisons may only FALL — new client role-gates must use window.WHRoles.isSupervisor()/.can(); wh-roles.js is the SSOT)
Truth-View Consumer-Columns (forward-only: no NEW consumer reads a column absent from the v_*_truth view it queries — catches PROJ-DRIFT)

Attribution integrity (every CLIENT insert/upsert into an auth_uid-no-default table must set auth_uid — locks the auth_uid-drop bug class found live 2026-07-06 on inventory_transactions/pm-scheduler/logbook/integrations/marketplace-seller/asset-hub; unresolvable payloads need an attribution-allow marker)

Client singleton / idle-refresh (every Supabase client routes through getDb() so it inherits the Finding-#6 token auto-refresh + visibilitychange refresh + timeout fetch and does not spawn a 2nd GoTrueClient — locks the raw-createClient idle-401 class found live 2026-07-06 on voice-handler.js/search-overlay.js; standalone public pages carry a singleton-exempt marker; dim-14)

Embed-auth / tenancy-gated edge-fn JWT forwarding (every browser fetch to embed-entry forwards the user session JWT as Bearer so its Pillar I tenancy check resolves — locks the client-drops-JWT 401 class found live 2026-07-07 on skillmatrix/logbook/pm-scheduler/voice-handler; without it the write lands but the skill/fault/PM embedding is silently dropped from the RAG index; dim-4)

Voice-journal single-write (the companion agent:'voice-journal' gateway call already persists the turn server-side via persistJournalEntry with an embedding — so NO client _saveJournalTurn/insert may run on its success or clarify path; locks the double-write class found+proven-live 2026-07-07 on voice-handler.js where every companion voice turn was journaled twice, one copy embedding-less; client saves belong only on non-gateway paths [shortcuts / RAG short-circuit / offline catch]; dim-4)

Read ceiling (2026-10-28, found by the first cube walk): no served page or script asks one response for more rows than the API sends (PostgREST max_rows 1,000). .limit(2000) read 1,000 and every .limit(N + 1) probe past 1,000 never received its row - achievements showed +20,120 XP for 39,760 with no 'At least', and inventory would have dropped every part past the 1,000th. A larger read is asked a page at a time (utils.js whReadPaged). Comments blanked; RPC p_limit included. Self-test: --self-test (7 cases).

Probe identities resolve (2026-10-28, found from a GitGuardian alert): a probe or prover acts as a person it LOOKS UP, never as a literal account id. Eight bank probes and four provers named their worker, supervisor, outsider and project by literal uuids; the clean reseed recreated every one, so a supervisor's legitimate write read BLOCKED, change orders broke their foreign key, two provers could not run, and the same literal reached the public repo and was mailed to Ian as a leaked 'secret' (a dead test-account id - no credential). Flags a random uuid in a JWT sub, an auth_uid = filter, or a uid:/UID_* constant; a synthetic fixture id (six repeated digits) and an account the file creates are legal. Self-test: --self-test (8 cases).

CA (Caching/CDN) deep-walk cell — every page in the service-worker OFFLINE SHELL (sw.js SHELL_FILES) must (a) exist on disk (a stale entry 404s the SW precache install → the whole offline shell breaks for every PWA user) and (b) the shell must be cache-VERSIONED (CACHE_NAME), so a shell change re-primes rather than serving stale cached markup. Emits its exact per-page pass-list to deepwalk_layer_pages.json[CA] for the deepwalk flywheel's CA architectural-layer cell (the gate-emitted-pass-list mechanism: the gate publishes its EXACT scope, the flywheel never regex-approximates). 8 shell HTML pages. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

PUSH HANDLER CONTRACT — a delivered push must actually reach the person. FOUND 2026-07-30 while dispositioning the test bank's TB-S5-edge-push-delivery-roundtrip cell, whose note read 'nothing proves a real subscription RENDERS the notification'. Checked rather than assumed: the SEND side is well covered (notify-push is VAPID-signed and was proven E2E against the real FCM service) and TWO service-worker validators already exist — validate_sw_offline and validate_sw_shell_membership — but NEITHER mentions push, showNotification or notificationclick even once. The receive side had no gate at all. That gap matters because every failure mode is SILENT, and sw.js says so itself: 'Without these handlers a delivered push silently no-ops.' The push arrives, the worker wakes, nothing appears, and nothing errors anywhere a person or a log would see it — a provider just misses the job. SEVEN invariants, each a silent failure: (1) a `push` listener exists (else the push is delivered and discarded); (2) the handler calls showNotification (else the worker wakes and renders nothing); (3) that call is INSIDE event.waitUntil — brace-matched, and the check requires waitUntil to WRAP it rather than merely appear in the handler, because a bare showNotification works on a warm worker and fails on a cold one, which is the hardest kind of bug to reproduce; (4) e.data.json() is guarded by try/catch, since a non-JSON payload THROWS and one malformed push then silently suppresses the notification; (5) a `notificationclick` listener exists (else the tap does nothing); (6) it focuses a tab or opens one (else the notification is a dead end); (7) it closes the notification (else the tray keeps an item the user already acted on). Static by design — these are properties of the file that ships to installed PWAs, and the CACHE_NAME comment records the cost of getting it wrong: 'without this bump installed PWAs keep the handler-less worker'. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: the OS notification tray is outside any harness, so 'the human saw it' stays unprobeable; the runtime tier (dispatch a push event to a registered worker and assert showNotification fired) remains recorded as owed with this gate named as its first half, so the residual gap has a shape instead of a shrug. Self-test proves all 7 hold on the shipped worker AND that five deliberately broken workers are each caught.

SERVICE_HAILING itemized execution audit (Ian 2026-07-29: 'itemize everything written in the roadmap, then check one by one if we have executed it'). 85 concrete promises - every Fuel table, Engine view/RPC, Brain agent, Dashboard surface, stack layer, §1c booster, C1-C11 lock, §3 dimension, G1-G4 gap, phase deliverable, D1-D14 decision and safety rail - each re-derived from the LIVE database, filesystem and gate registry, never from a hand-kept checklist. FAILs naming any promise that stops being true.

T82: edge refusals reach the user — the static census. supabase-js collapses EVERY non-2xx from functions.invoke into ONE FunctionsHttpError whose message is the literal string "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code". The status and body survive only on error.context (a Response), so a caller reading error.message never sees them - and shows that placeholder to a person. ★THE CLIENT THEN SILENTLY UNDOES THE WORK THE BACKEND DID: rate-limit.ts answers a drained hive with 429 and "AI call limit reached for this hive. Try again in an hour." - cause named, clearing time named, exactly the bar the AI-error taxonomy exists to hold. MEASURED on asset-hub (met by genuinely exhausting the hourly quota): the worker read "Could not reach Asset Brain: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code", a CONNECTION-flavoured sentence for a QUOTA event, sending them to check their signal instead of waiting an hour. whAiError could not rescue it either - it keys on /429|rate.?limit|quota/ and the placeholder carries none of them. Fixed centrally: utils.js whFnError() reads error.context, so the function's own sentence survives and only a body-less failure falls back to the status taxonomy. The unwrap had been hand-rolled in companion-launcher, analytics and assistant - three copies, thirteen other files without it. WHAT IT COUNTS: invoke error branches that put error.message in front of a person (toast, innerHTML, textContent, a whListError/whReadError call) without consulting error.context or whFnError. ★IT COUNTS RATHER THAN FORBIDS - 39 invoke sites, 19 speaking the placeholder at first measure; a gate that failed all of them on day one would be turned off. Forward-only against tools/edge_refusal_baseline.json; asset-hub's four sites were cleared in the same pass, 19 -> 16. ★AND IT ONLY FLAGS BRANCHES THAT SPEAK: an invoke whose error is logged, swallowed or rethrown shows nobody the placeholder, and charging for it would measure code shape rather than harm.

T89: converted money states its rate — the owner's AI-cost oracle (2026-08-26). ai-quality's cost card is the owner's answer to 'what is this costing me'. Every peso figure on it - the hero, the per-call average, and the MODEST / TYPICAL / HEAVY verdict thresholds - came from one hardcoded constant, PHP_PER_USD = 56, which was neither dated nor shown. PHP/USD has moved between roughly 50 and 59 in recent years, so a drifting rate silently shifts both the number and the JUDGEMENT about it, while the card reads like a measurement. The figure is not so much wrong as unfalsifiable: an owner cannot tell whether ₱2,100 means 'heavy use' or 'the rate is stale'. The rate is now stated beside the figure, the way a source chip states a window. ★IT DOES NOT DEMAND A LIVE RATE - a fixed rate is a reasonable choice for a cost estimate; presenting the result as if nothing was assumed is not. Checked and found CORRECT rather than manufactured into a defect: the conversion itself is sound (php = totalCost * PHP_PER_USD, and the thresholds compare pesos to pesos), and the details table's USD figure is labelled as USD. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the rate is undisclosed and the gate names the line.

T89: the quota warns before the wall — a count is not a warning (2026-08-26). _shared/rate-limit.ts returns `remaining` on EVERY allowed call, so the platform always knows how close a hive is to its hourly cap. NOTHING CONSUMED IT: there is no threshold anywhere in the codebase, and the only signal a worker ever got was the 429 AFTER the wall - mid-task, with the work half done. asset-hub was the single surface rendering the number at all, and it rendered it flat ('12 AI calls remaining this hour'), which reads the same at 12 as at 1. whQuotaNotice() now turns the number the server already sends into a warning at 5 or fewer and names the reset, so 'wait' has a 'how long'. ★THE UNKNOWN CASE WAS A BUG IN THE FIRST VERSION, caught by exercising the shipped helper rather than trusting it: Number(null) is 0, so a quota the server did not report was announced as 'No AI calls left this hour' - absence rendered as a value, alarming and false. An absent reading is not a reading of zero; it is now silent. ★IT DOES NOT REQUIRE EVERY AI SURFACE TO SHOW A QUOTA - most never receive `remaining`, and demanding that plumbing everywhere would make this a migration rather than a gate; it holds the surfaces that DO show it to showing it usefully. ★AND ITS OWN MATCHER WAS BLIND FIRST: it looked for 'whQuotaNotice(' while utils.js defines it as 'whQuotaNotice = function', so it reported the helper missing while it sat ten lines above - it would have failed forever on a correct file. Teeth: pre-fix it flags both the bare render and the absent helper.

T121 (2026-08-28): a dismissal is a person's decision, not the browser's. The shared station tablet is this platform's normal deployment - one device, a crew signing in and out through a shift - and three dismissal flags stored the literal string '1', which belongs to the BROWSER: wh_onboarding_dismissed (index's first-run Getting Started ladder), wh_cmms_guide_dismissed (integrations' setup guide), and wh_guide_link_dismissed_<page> (learn-link's 'New to this page?' chip, which rides EVERY page). Worker A taps Dismiss; worker B signs in on the same tablet and is never introduced to anything. ★THIS LEAK RUNS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM ITS SIBLINGS, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED THEM: the draft, filter and companion-history fixes all stopped A's CONTENT reaching B, so they read as privacy work and this did not - nothing of A's is exposed. What crosses is A's DECISION, and the cost lands on B as an ABSENCE: no card, no chip, nothing on screen to notice or report. The onboarding ladder made it sharper still - its three step-checks were ALREADY person-aware (workerName, jobs, pmDoneToday), so the card knew B had done nothing; it just never got to run, because the flag returned before the check. Correct logic behind a device-wide gate. Fixed centrally (whStateOwner/whIsDismissed/whSetDismissed in utils.js, replacing a FOURTH hand-rolled owner read) and at all three sites; a legacy '1' is nobody's, so the guide returns once - for HELP that is the safe direction, since re-showing a card costs a tap and hiding it costs the introduction. sessionStorage flags are exempt: they die with the tab. Live-proven at 390 (A dismissed -> B sees the guide -> A still dismissed -> legacy '1' belongs to no one), probe restoring the real owner it captured first. Selftest 9/9, including two non-vacuity checks: the first versions of both negatives swapped only the helper CALL, leaving the typeof guard inside the exemption window, so they passed while detecting nothing.

T99: a comma in a search box must not 400 the read (2026-08-26). MEASURED against the live REST endpoint: or=(machine.ilike.*bearing, spherical*,...) returns HTTP 400, 'failed to parse logic tree'. PostgREST's or=(a,b) grammar splits on top-level commas, so an unquoted comma inside a value ends the condition early and the ENTIRE filter is rejected; parentheses do the same. ★THE TERM THAT BREAKS IT IS THE ORDINARY ONE: 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF' is how a real part is named - it is this platform's OWN example in the longest-truncates gate - and typing it into the logbook feed, the logbook EXPORT, community, or the global search overlay produced a 400 the page renders as a FAILED READ. A legitimate search looked like an outage, which is worse than no results: the worker concludes the system is down and stops looking. ★TWO DIFFERENT JOBS, AND ONLY ONE WAS BEING DONE. Escaping % and _ stops a wildcard changing WHICH rows match; removing the delimiters stops the filter failing to parse at all. FOUR sites did the first and not the second. marketplace.html was the exception - it strips them - which is why the same phrase worked there and nowhere else, and why nobody had noticed. ★FIXED CENTRALLY with whSafeSearchTerm (delimiters removed, wildcards escaped, capped), applied at all four sites. Delimiters are REMOVED rather than escaped because PostgREST offers no escape for them inside an unquoted value, and a space keeps word boundaries so the phrase still matches. VERIFIED END TO END: the same read that returned 400 now returns 200 with an empty array - an honest no-match instead of an error. ★AND THE SAME BUG WAS IN THE EDGE FUNCTIONS, where it is WORSE because it is SILENT. agentic-rag-loop's logbook lane sanitises a natural-language QUESTION - where commas are not an edge case but the common case - and read the result as `const { data: logs } = await q`, DESTRUCTURING THE ERROR AWAY. supabase-js RETURNS {data:null,error} rather than throwing, so the rejected filter never reached the surrounding catch and `logs || []` turned a 400 into an ordinary empty result: the AI answered with less grounding and nothing anywhere said why. Its comment reads 'Escape LIKE wildcards in user input (per data-engineer skill)' - the author followed the skill exactly, and the skill covered wildcards but not delimiters. visual-defect-capture passed an asset TAG into an .or() with no escaping at all. Both fixed, and the error is now logged instead of discarded. The gate covers the edge functions too, including the `const { data } = await q` shape that makes the failure invisible. Teeth proven on four clauses: the helper weakened, a page interpolating a raw term, an edge fn dropping the delimiter strip, and an edge fn discarding the error again.

T28: an audit nobody can reach is write-only (2026-08-27). 'Who changed this?' is asked while looking at the RECORD - an asset whose details are wrong, a reported post, a decision someone disputes. If the only way in is to know the page exists and open it cold, the trail is technically complete and practically useless: the supervisor gives up or goes to SQL, and the compliance story the platform tells about itself is one nobody can walk. ★A LINK THAT DROPS THE RECORD IS BARELY BETTER - arriving at an unfiltered log of every power action while holding the id in your head is the same scavenger hunt with extra steps. So BOTH ends are asserted: the links must carry the subject (asset-hub sends ?q=<tag>, community sends ?action=report_post) AND audit-log must CONSUME those parameters, or the context is written into the URL and thrown away - a promise only the sender believes, which is the declared-but-never-wired class. MEASURED: two context-carrying links, audit-log consumes all four of q/actor/action/target. ★THE HIVE MENU ENTRY DOES NOT SATISFY THIS: audit-log is a hidden page, so a menu item makes it reachable only to someone who already knows to look; the record-level affordances are what make it findable at the moment the question is actually asked, which is why bare links are reported but do not count toward the requirement. Teeth proven on both halves - links stripped of their record, and the audit page ceasing to read what it is sent.

W46181: an article may only tell a reader to press a control that EXISTS. learn/philippine-plants-now-pay-the-highest-power-rates measured perfect on every design instrument - contrastLow 0 across 163 nodes, rhythmOffGrid 0, 10 headings with 0 skips - while instructing the reader five times, in numbered steps, to press a '⚡ Electrical 14' button and claiming the tool 'flags any machine over the limit', 'pulls the DOE’s current rate' and 'applies the RA 11285 audit rule'. None of it exists. The string 'Electrical 14' occurs ONCE in the repository: inside an HTML COMMENT in engineering-design.html listing discipline counts. An LLM read the comment and promoted it to a button. ★THE GUARD THAT ALREADY EXISTED WAS AIMED AT THE CHEAPER SURFACE: tools/topic_post.py has a real, self-tested fabrication guard (numbers_sourced traces every figure back to Ian’s notes, and it earned its place on run one by catching an invented '11.8 cent per kilowatt-hour' in the wrong currency) - but it runs on the FACEBOOK CAPTION. The /learn article, the surface that is indexed, mirrored into a markdown twin and quoted by answer engines, went out through scaffold_article with no equivalent check. The ephemeral thing was guarded and the permanent one was not. ★THIS GATE STRIPS COMMENTS, which IS the point: its own teeth test failed at first because 'Electrical 14' IS in the repo, in that comment - a gate that reads comments is fooled by the same text that fooled the model. Then stripping them naively reported a REAL button as invented, because accept="image/*" opened a false /*…*/ that ate 10,553 characters of resume.html - this project’s own recorded lesson, reproduced verbatim while writing the gate to prevent fabrication. Both are pinned by assertions. SCOPE, stated honestly: it proves a NAMED CONTROL exists, nothing more - not that a statistic is real (authority-links checks the citation resolves), not that arithmetic is sound (the same page claimed a 500-kW boiler room drawing 12 kWh an hour saved ₱3,000 a day, off by ~10x). Registers GREEN at 21 controls across 5 articles, so it is a ratchet, not a backlog. Costs 0.9s. MK13 - reachable capability: a page that LISTS table T and shows a forward-looking empty state ("they will appear here") must have some client path that can INSERT into T, or the empty state is promising a capability the product does not have. A role-derived class on a PERSISTENT ROOT (<html>/<body>) must be removable — if a page adds one, it must also remove it on the path where the role is lost. Found live 2026-07-27 (hive deepwalk H8, remove-member): hive.html painted `html.is-supervisor` early from the CACHED role, deliberately, so supervisor-only chrome would not flash in after the async membership check (a CLS optimisation) — and nothing ever cleared it. Deleting a member's row left her browser carrying a supervisor marker on <html> with no supervisor membership behind it. Harmless ONLY because the board never renders for a removed member; the moment any supervisor-only rule keys off that class on a view a removed member CAN reach, it misapplies. Root elements are the whole point: unlike a card or a button they survive every view switch and re-render, so the removal has to be written, never inherited from a re-render. Verified as an instrument, not assumed — run against the pre-fix hive.html it FAILS on `is-supervisor`, against the fix it passes. Deliberately narrow so a PASS means something: only documentElement/body targets, only role-vocabulary names (so button-lock's `is-loading` is out of scope), and toggle() counts as a removal since it is add-and-remove by construction. This is HK1's SECOND assertion only; the first (a hidden element must be EMPTY, not display:none over real data) is a DOM property the live deepwalk checks, and folding it in here would let a static PASS imply a live guarantee it never made. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

A page may adopt the canonical role (`wh_hive_role`) from exactly ONE place. Adopting a role is not one assignment — it is the module variable, the stored hint, AND any paint derived from it, which must move together. Found live 2026-07-27 (hive deepwalk H8b/H8d/H3): hive.html had SEVEN role-adoption sites and only TWO repainted `html.is-supervisor`, whose rules are FUNCTIONAL not cosmetic (they set `#my-work-card{display:none}` and hide `#pm-overdue-alert` / `#stock-alert`). Each unreconciled site was its own door onto the same defect and THREE were confirmed live before being fixed: DEMOTION (role synced down, marker stayed, so a demoted worker lost their own work card and their overdue-PM and stock alerts while the page looked normal), SWITCH (a switch never reloads — it calls initBoard() in place — so the page-load fix never ran), and JOIN (joining a hive where you are a worker while holding supervisor paint from another). The lesson is not 'remember to repaint' but that a value with invariants attached needs ONE adopter, so the invariant is written once instead of remembered seven times; hive.html now routes everything through applyHiveRole(). Verified as an instrument rather than assumed: against pre-centralization hive.html it FAILS with 7 sites (lines 1807/1911/1980/2119/2256/2270/5234), against the fix it passes with 1. Reads are deliberately not counted — counting them would fail every page on the platform — and scan/test harnesses that plant a role to set up a scenario are exempt. Static/fast. Self-test: --selftest.

Every read and write names a column its table actually has (static, substrate-backed). supabase-js does NOT throw when PostgREST refuses a row - it resolves with { error } - so a wrong column name fails in the quietest way available. Found FIVE in voice-handler.js: three spelled `event_type` where ai_audit_log's column is `event`, one wrote `source` to a table with no such column, and the fifth - the only one on a LIVE path - wrote `negative_count` where ai_quality_escalation has `thumbs_down_7d`, so the supervisor-outreach flag had never once been set. The READ side found its own: worker-drawer selected `reorder_point` from inventory_items, a column the platform KNOWS is absent (migration 20260510000003 created v_inventory_items_truth to alias it), so the drawer always said 'No low-stock items assigned' on a read that returned 400. Reads inline write objects AND `.insert(row)` where the object is built above; anything it cannot parse honestly is SKIPPED and counted.

Column-name gate teeth (13 cases): a wrong column caught inline and via an object built above, update/upsert/select all read, the nearest-declaration rule that its own first bug broke, and spread/shorthand/wildcard/unknown-table all skipped rather than guessed.

Is the AI companion's certified capability REACHED? Twenty validate_ai_companion_*.py files guard voice-handler.js and every check they make asks whether a NAME IS SPELLED IN THE SOURCE. Measured: 283 symbols guarded, 154 never called inside the file, 71 never called ANYWHERE. Four were opened by hand and all four were also WRONG - the erasure the assistant offers and never performed, the audit row 'every confirmed write action' never wrote, a 180-day retention that never aged anything out, and a compliance export nobody could produce. Never exercised, so the mistake kept. Forward-only ratchet; --list names them.

SW install survives a lost request (10 cases): install ran cache.addAll(SHELL_FILES), which is ATOMIC - one failed entry rejects, the rejection escapes waitUntil, and the worker goes from `installing` to `redundant`, leaving the person with NO service worker at all (no precache, no offline fallback, no network-first page copy) and nothing anywhere saying so. Found 2026-09-10 by asking a browser whether the worker actually CONTROLS the pages a journey walks: under the prover's own offline-3g emulation it returned `registered:true, state:installing, finalState:REDUNDANT` with sw.js itself never dropped, while the same page with routing but no drops installed normally - so the loss killed it, not the instrumentation. Not merely a stress-test concern: the install survives only if all 65 entries land, so at 1-in-12 that is 0.35%, at an ordinary 1% request loss it is (0.99)^65 = 52% (half of real plant-floor installs failing completely), and at 3% it is 14%. Each entry now gets one retry and a file that still will not come is left out rather than taking the install down with it; verified live afterwards - WITH drops the worker reaches `activated` with 65/65 cached, where before it went redundant with zero. Both directions pinned and mutation-tested four ways: restore the atomic addAll, smuggle an addAll in beside the tolerant path, drop the per-file catch, or precache only a hand-picked few, and each is caught.
